nativeCoverage: Persistent files survive context disposal and a fully stopped Worker runtime before replacement.
Each context receives its current host callbacks without serializing caller capabilities.
A grant without manage permission can execute; a readonly grant cannot modify files.
An 8 MiB context rejects a 20 MB allocation while a 32 MiB context succeeds.
The persisted sandbox memory ceiling overrides a larger context request.
Closing a context cancels and observes its active execution without cancelling another queued process.
A callback accepted before closure may settle; subsequent host effects are denied.
limitations: Remote persistent RPC and a real Minutei model turn remain unverified.
Minutei still selects ephemeral contexts; persistent agent and tenant lifecycle is not integrated.
JavaScript heaps and host callbacks are not restored across executions.
Capability renewal and final disposal belong to the persistent sandbox owner.
Terminal receipt observation does not roll back previously accepted external effects or promise immediate CPU termination.
No cost or performance comparison with AgentOS is established.
